tldr: This survey establishes agentic reasoning as a unifying paradigm that reframes LLMs from passive sequence predictors into autonomous agents that plan, act, and learn through continual interaction with their environment.
contributions: A systematic taxonomy organizing agentic reasoning along three layers of environmental dynamics: foundational single-agent capabilities, self-evolving adaptation, and collective multi-agent collaboration
A dual-axis analysis distinguishing in-context reasoning (inference-time orchestration) from post-training reasoning (reinforcement learning and fine-tuning)
A formal control-theoretic framework using POMDPs to unify the transition from static language modeling to agentic reasoning
A comprehensive review of real-world applications and benchmarks spanning science, robotics, healthcare, autonomous research, and mathematics
Identification of open challenges including personalization, long-horizon interaction, world modeling, scalable multi-agent training, and governance frameworks
methods: The paper synthesizes existing agentic reasoning work through a structured taxonomy built on a formal Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) framework, factorizing agent policies into internal reasoning and external action components. It categorizes planning approaches into six methodological styles including workflow design, tree search, and algorithm simulation, and analyzes optimization mechanisms across in-context search methods (e.g., ReAct, Tree-of-Thoughts, MCTS) and post-training approaches (e.g., GRPO-based RL). The survey further examines multi-agent reasoning formalized as decentralized POMDPs with communication channels.
results: The survey maps how agentic reasoning bridges thought and action across three environmental layers: foundational agents use planning, tool use, and search in stable environments; self-evolving agents integrate feedback and memory through mechanisms like Reflexion and RL-for-memory; and collective agents coordinate through role assignment and shared memory. In-context reasoning scales test-time interaction without modifying parameters, while post-training reasoning consolidates capabilities into model weights. Key frameworks reviewed include ReAct, ToT, GRPO/ARPO/DAPO, AutoGen, CAMEL, GPTSwarm, and OpenHands. Limitations noted include error accumulation over long horizons and challenges in communication efficiency, stability, and trustworthiness in multi-agent systems.
limitations: Error accumulation over long horizons in workflows; challenges in stability, communication efficiency, and trustworthiness for multi-agent systems; lack of rigorous evaluation standards; and unresolved issues around personalization, long-horizon interaction, world modeling, scalable multi-agent training, and governance frameworks for real-world deployment.
